excerpt: Kane CLI from TestMu AI (formerly LambdaTest) runs browser tests written in plain English from your terminal, with evidence packs, headless CI mode, Playwright export and a Claude Code skill. Free CLI and local runs; plans from $19 a month. How it works and alternatives.
content:
Kane CLI is a command-line testing agent from TestMu AI, the company formerly known as LambdaTest. You describe a flow in plain English, such as logging in as an admin, opening billing and checking the plan, and Kane CLI drives a real Chrome browser through it and reports pass or fail. There are no selectors to maintain and no custom test language. Each run produces a portable evidence pack with screenshots, step logs and a pass or fail verdict for each criterion, and flows can be exported as native Playwright scripts.

It installs from npm, has a visible mode for debugging and a headless mode for CI that use the same test, and an agent flag that outputs structured NDJSON so coding agents such as Claude Code, Cursor, ChatGPT or Gemini can call it; a Kane CLI skill is available for Claude Code. In June 2026 TestMu AI added a generate command that turns a described feature or workflow into structured test cases saved as reusable .testmd files.

The Kane CLI launch was TestMu AI's fourteenth on Product Hunt. It went live on 13 August 2026 and finished #1 for the day with 421 upvotes and 56 comments.

We have not tested Kane CLI ourselves. This page brings together TestMu AI's Kane CLI page and press release, its Product Hunt page, and says where each fact comes from.

profile.platform: Command line (npm), runs Chrome locally or on TestMu AI's cloud
profile.starts_at: Free CLI and local runs; plans from $19/month
profile.summary_short: Terminal agent that runs browser tests written in plain English and returns evidence packs
use_cases: Writing end-to-end browser tests in plain English instead of selectors
Running the same test visibly while debugging and headless in CI
Letting Claude Code or another coding agent test the app it just changed
Generating test cases from a feature description
Exporting flows to Playwright when you need code

fit: are a developer or QA engineer tired of brittle selector-based tests
use coding agents and want them to verify changes in a real browser
already use TestMu AI (LambdaTest) for cloud testing
not_fit: need native mobile app testing from this page's documented features: the official page describes Chrome browser testing
want no account at all: execution goes through a TestMu AI account
need large volumes of cloud runs on the free plan's 200 credits

pricing.intro: The CLI is free to install and local runs are free; cloud runs are billed against a TestMu AI plan. Prices are in US dollars from the Kane CLI page.
notes: Launch bonus credits applied for the first three months on paid plans.

alternatives.intro: Product Hunt lists QA.tech, TestSprite and DogQ among the alternatives. Review scores are Product Hunt users' own; check each tool's pricing page for current prices.

items.name: QA.tech
items.what: AI agents that create and run QA tests
items.difference: A hosted agent that explores and tests your app; Kane CLI runs from your terminal and CI.

items.name: TestSprite
items.difference: Also aimed at AI coding workflows; compare its MCP-based approach with Kane CLI's terminal agent.

items.name: DogQ
items.what: Testing tool that writes, heals and suggests tests
items.difference: A no-code web interface rather than a command-line tool.

alternatives.more: Product Hunt also lists QApilot and Testpine.

pros: Tests in plain English, without selectors or a custom language
Evidence pack with screenshots and per-step logs for every run
Same test runs visible or headless in CI
Works with coding agents through structured output and a Claude Code skill
cons: Needs a TestMu AI account; cloud runs use plan credits
Free plan has 200 credits a month
Natural-language tests can be less precise than coded assertions
Product Hunt reviews cover TestMu AI's wider product line, not Kane CLI alone

x.none: We found no posts about Kane CLI on X to link yet.

faq.a: A command-line agent from TestMu AI that runs browser tests written in plain English in a real Chrome browser and reports pass or fail with evidence.
Run npm install -g @testmuai/kane-cli, check it with kane-cli --version, then sign in with kane-cli login (or kane-cli setup for headless environments).
The CLI and local runs are free. Cloud runs use your TestMu AI plan: free with 200 credits, Starter $19 or Pro $99 a month.
Yes. An agent flag outputs structured NDJSON, and there is a Kane CLI skill for Claude Code.
Product Hunt lists QApilot, DogQ, Testpine, QA.tech and TestSprite.
